newsitem.title: INDIA: Gujral says India can achieve 8.0 pct growth rate.
newsitem.headline: Gujral says India can achieve 8.0 pct growth rate.

text.p: Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said on Thursday that India can achieve a buoyant eight percent economic growth rate and expressed confidence there would be an increased inflow of foreign direct investment.

"I think India is on the march to take our rate of growth to eight percent from seven percent," Gujral said in an interview on the state-run Doordarshan television. "And I see no reason why we should not reach it," he said.
India hopes to achieve 6.8 percent growth in gross domestic product in 1996/97 (April-March) compared with 7.1 percent in the previous year.
Gujral said he would call a meeting of all political parties to discuss the pathbreaking 1997/98 budget proposals.

The government would consider amendments suggested by the left-wing parties and the main opposition Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), he said. But he reiterated that the direction of the budget will be "intact".
The budget, widely hailed by industry and foreign investors, proposes to cut income and corporate taxes and reduce import tariffs.
Gujral said the United Front government has attracted $3.0 billion of foreign direct investment since taking office in June last year, compared with $2.0 billion in the previous three years.
"And also there is more confidence in our economy," Gujral added.

But he warned that his government needed to take a bold decision to contain the oil pool deficit resulting from the gap between free market oil prices and the subsidised prices, fixed by the state, at which oil is sold by the refineries.
"That is unavoidable," he said in response to a question on the oil pool deficit. "It is an unfortunate part of government that sometimes bold decisions will have to be taken," he said.

"We will try to soften the blow as much as we can," Gujral said. Analysts say pressure was mounting on the government to raise petroleum product prices to tackle the burgeoning oil pool deficit, estimated at 155 billion rupees ($4.3 billion) for 1996/97.
The prime minister said the government would safeguard the interests of the poorer sections of society and provide subsidies to meet their needs.
Gujral also said he was prepared to work towards resolving all outstanding issues with arch-rival Pakistan through dialogue.
Gujral and his Pakistani counterpart Nawaz Sharief will hold talks on May 12 ahead of a South Asian Association of Regional Cooperation (SAARC) summit in Maldives.
The meeting would follow two rounds of high-level talks that resumed in March after three years of recriminations between the longstanding foes.
